title: Per-run environment for declared test commands without committing machine-specific values (e.g. SUPABASE_TEST_URL)
outcome:
A repository can declare a test command that needs a machine-specific environment value, such as Comovo's integration suite, which reads SUPABASE_TEST_URL. The value is supplied per machine without being committed and without global configuration changes, and the declared run stays exactly matchable and creditable.

Today a declared line cannot carry `VAR=value`. An `env VAR=value …` line would commit the value. TermAl neither captures nor injects the agent shell's environment, and Claude's Bash tool doesn't keep exported variables between calls. Greg's side (Asistant #942) forbids hard-coding the current local port.
acceptance: Before implementation, a short design is recorded and agreed with Kimi::Consultant. It names the smallest supported mechanism, reusing existing project or session configuration where possible, through which a declared run receives named per-machine environment values that live outside the repository. It also states how matching, the source identity and the artifact verdict stay unchanged, and why no value is committed or made global.

The implemented mechanism lets a declared entry obtain such a value at run time on one machine, with deterministic tests. A missing value refuses or flags the run with a named reason instead of silently falling back to a default. The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact committed input.

completion.summary: Local per-machine project environment for declared commands landed in combo16, with applied runtime selection, names-only binding, missing-name verdicts, deterministic author tests, clean required reviews and exact-tree landing FULLs.
